subject: Provisioning plan: reserved GPU pool, PHI isolation, and SLO targets
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleanor Kim <eleanor.kim@citymed.ai>, platformops@citymed.ai
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Provisioning plan: reserved GPU pool, PHI isolation, and SLO targets

Hi Eleanor / CityMed team,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to see the end-to-end flow for your clinical assistant. Below is a short recap, our assumptions, and the immediate next steps so we can scope a dedicated-reservation proposal for you.

Key pain points you called out
- PHI handling: all inference must run in an isolated VPC with strict egress controls and KMS-managed keys; SSO for operator accounts.
- Predictable latency: peak inference path needs predictable 95th-percentile latency for short requests (under 350 ms) and acceptable tails for longer multimodal prompts.
- Burst behavior: periodic nightly batches and weekly peaks during QA runs; need predictable isolation so other tenants won't affect throughput.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement wants a clear monthly commitment vs burst pricing and an ops playbook for fallback.

Goals we agreed on
- Dedicated pool with tenant isolation (no co-tenancy) and VPC-only access.
- Baseline throughput target: 200 concurrent inference streams with median latency ~60–120 ms (model dependent); 95th percentile <350 ms for standard prompts.
- Autoscale/burst to handle 2x baseline for short windows (operational bursts, QA jobs).
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool; regional failover plan for critical windows.

Initial sizing & proposal (high level)
- Reserve 4x GPU units (A100-class equivalence) for baseline, burst to 6 units in reserved burst capacity.
- Isolation: dedicated tenant (no shared pods), private subnet in your VPC, customer-managed KMS, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
- Canary rollout: start with a small canary partition (10% traffic) and ramp over 2 weeks.
- Estimated starting price (ballpark): USD 38k–45k/month (subject to final model footprint and run-hours).

Attachments: I attached a short scope doc and an SLA draft for your legal/procurement review. I also included a simple pricing workbook.

Immediate next steps
1) Please confirm data residency: US-only is required? (you indicated yes — confirm in reply).
2) Share token/throughput profile: average tokens/request and expected batch/sequence length for the most common flows.
3) We'll schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi (infra) and our ops lead to validate model footprint and autoscaling policies.
4) Procurement: once scope is agreed we'll issue a formal quote and MSA/DocuSign path.

Proposed times for technical call: Wed 6/3 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 6/4 9:00–10:00 PT — let me know what works.

Thanks,

Jordan
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Provisioning plan: reserved GPU pool, PHI isolation, and SLO targets

Jordan,

Thanks for the clear recap — very helpful. A few quick clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Residency: yes, US-only; all PHI must remain within our US VPC and logs stored in our SIEM (Splunk).
- Security: please include our security contact (sec-ops@citymed.ai) on the next package; they will need to review SOC2 evidence and KMS integration details.
- Pricing: the ballpark looks reasonable but can you provide a breakdown per-GPU and per-hour burst rate so procurement can model multiple scenarios?
- Timing: we are trying to get an internal PO approved by the end of June to hit Q3 pilots — if we can lock a scope this week that would help.

I'll loop in our procurement lead (cc'd) and sec-ops. For the technical deep-dive, Wed 6/3 10:00 PT works for us.

—Eleanor
Eleanor Kim
Head of Platform Engineering | CityMed AI
eleanor.kim@citymed.ai

Subject: Re: Provisioning plan: reserved GPU pool, PHI isolation, and SLO targets

Jordan — looping in Rishi for capacity/ops planning. A few operational asks so we can come prepared to Wed's deep-dive:

- Please get CityMed to send representative payloads (token distribution) and a sample of peak hourly qps over a typical week.
- Confirm whether you need persistent KV-cache across requests for chat workloads (that changes memory/instance sizing).
- We'll prepare an isolation runbook (network ACLs, IAM roles, KMS flow) and a canary playbook that includes rollback thresholds and automated fallback to a hosted model.
- Rishi: can you draft a small matrix of GPU counts vs expected steady qps and 95th latency targets for the most common model families? I can attach that to the scope doc.

Neha — please include this in the HubSpot deal and start procurement templating.

Thanks,
Avery
